Subject: Discovery recap: tool calling + structured JSON outputs for AtlasCard

Hi Eleanor,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Really appreciate the open conversation - bringing this thread to capture what we heard and the immediate next steps. Please let me know if I missed or misstated anything.

Quick summary of pain points you shared:
- Multiple downstream systems (fraud engine, reconciliation, reporting) require deterministic JSON schemas; current LLM outputs vary and break parsers.
- You have frequent format regressions when prompt changes occur; manual QA is slow and brittle.
- Latency and throughput constraints: some reconciliation calls need <300ms P95 to be practical in the transaction path.
- Traceability / auditability: outputs and tool calls must be logged with correlation ids for compliance.

Current stack you described:
- Internal microservices in Go (Postgres primary, Redis for caching)
- A small orchestration layer that triggers downstream jobs
- Some home-grown templating + validation that fails on model output skew

Success criteria you listed:
- Deterministic, schema-compliant JSON for tool/function calling 99%+ of the time for top-level keys
- Support for a compact, documented JSON Schema we can validate against (server-side)
- Sub-300ms P95 for simple tool calls (token-limited responses) and graceful degradation with a fallback model variant
- Audit logs for each call (input, output, model id, confidence/metadata)

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) I will share a proposed JSON Schema and an example agent workflow for the reconcile_transactions tool (attached).
2) Marissa (our Solutions Engineer) will run a short technical deep-dive to map the agent workflow to your infra and validate latency assumptions.
3) We schedule a 45-min tech-call next week to prototype one endpoint and agree on validation checkpoints.

Attachments: redwood-product-sheet.pdf (product one-pager), proposed-json-schema.json (draft schema + example payload)

Thanks - I copied Marissa so she can follow up with the technical details.

Best,

Subject: Proposed JSON Schema + agent workflow (draft)

Hi Eleanor,

Following up with a short draft of the JSON Schema we discussed and a recommended agent / tool-calling pattern. Full draft attached (proposed-json-schema.json) and I pasted a compact example below so you can get a feel quickly.

Agent workflow (high-level):
- User prompt -> Redwood runtime parses intent -> agent invokes tool: reconcile_transactions
- Tool call payload must match the JSON Schema below; Redwood will validate before invocation to guarantee deterministic structure
- Tool returns standard result object; runtime logs request/response with correlation_id and model metadata

Example tool call (pseudo):
{
  "tool": "reconcile_transactions",
  "args": {
    "batch_id": "string",
    "transactions": [
      {"id": "string", "amount_cents": 123, "currency": "USD", "timestamp": "2026-10-05T08:59:00Z"}
    ],
    "match_threshold": 0.95
  }
}

Draft JSON Schema (compact):
- type: object
- required: ["tool", "args"]
- properties:
  - tool: {type: "string", enum: ["reconcile_transactions"]}
  - args: {type: "object", required: ["batch_id","transactions"], properties: {batch_id: {type: "string"}, transactions: {type: "array", items: {type: "object", required: ["id","amount_cents","currency","timestamp"], properties: {id:{type:"string"}, amount_cents:{type:"integer"}, currency:{type:"string"}, timestamp:{type:"string", format:"date-time"}}}}, match_threshold: {type: "number", minimum: 0, maximum: 1}}

Deterministic formatting success criteria (what we'll validate):
- Output must strictly conform to the JSON Schema (server-side validation)
- No free-text top-level keys outside schema (deterministic keys only)
- If model produces invalid JSON, runtime should either correct via a constrained parser or fall back to a safe failure response with an error code we define
- P95 end-to-end (request -> tool invocation -> tool response) under 300ms for single-batch test (we will benchmark during the tech call)

Next steps I propose from here:
1) Eleanor: confirm a 45-min slot Tue/Wed next week for a tech deep-dive with your infra team.
2) Jordan: I'll run a short internal latency check against our staging model variants once we agree on a sample payload size.
3) Eleanor: please upload the sample reconciliation payloads to the Drive link and share the file name.

Happy to iterate the schema - the attached file has the same content but in canonical JSON.

Best,
Marissa Cole
